label: D2 after a2->S2 common, following a rewarded non-rare a2 trial (S2 streak), mid-episode
explanation: Fires only at D2 (100% of mass), and essentially only when the agent chose a2 and reached S2 via a common transition (in_action=2, in_state=2; base predicate recall 1.00, precision 0.38). Precision rises sharply when the previous trial was also a2 (stay) via a common transition and was rewarded, i.e. the agent is in a confirmed a2/S2-good streak; magnitude is highest in long runs of rewarded a2->S2c trials and in high-value / strongly-a2 policy steps (value >8.1 has 4.3x lift). It never fires at D1 or GO, on a1 or S1, on rare transitions, or after a switch. A strong, unexplained dependence on episode position: it is silent in trials 0-19 and 80-99 and active in 20-79, so ep_trial is included (without it F1 0.69). All variables are observed at D2; no future variables. Main misses are weak activations at the start of a streak or after a previous unrewarded trial.

issues: The claim that the unit needs the previous trial to be rewarded is too strict, and the misses it causes are systematic, not scattered. Take D2 a2->S2 common, stay, previous trial common, ep_trial 20-79. If the previous trial was unrewarded but the one before it was rewarded, precision is 0.78 (7745 predicted steps). The unit only shuts off after TWO unrewarded trials in a row (precision 0.24). Test-split misses show the pattern directly, e.g. '[-2] r1 a2 S2c | [-1] r0 a2 S2c:0.67'. Dropping prev_reward==1 altogether already beats the original on dev (F1 0.877 vs 0.866).

Requiring 'reward on either of the last two trials' instead of prev_reward==1 raises test F1 from 0.855 to 0.912 (P 0.91, R 0.914, mass recall 0.96). So the label 'following a rewarded ... a2 trial' misstates the condition. The real condition is a recent reward within roughly the last two trials of an unbroken a2->S2-common run.

The episode-position claim ('silent in trials 0-19 and 80-99, active 20-79') is a gradual ramp, not a step. Precision of the core predicate at single trials: t17 0.02, t19 0.14, t20 0.16, t22 0.39, t25 0.77, t75 0.73, t78 0.49, t80 0.20, t82 0.006. A 22..78 window does better than 20..79 (dev F1 0.888 vs 0.877 with stay/prev_common held fixed). The label's 'mid-episode' is fine, but the hard 20/80 boundaries overclaim.

Checks that hold up: active only at D2 (D1/GO 0 of 761k steps); never on a1, S1, or rare transitions (3 of 57967 active steps on a1/rare); essentially never after a switch (stay==0: 1 active step); prev_common==0 has rate 0.003. With those exclusions recall is about 1.0 at precision 0.38. No future variables are used.

Remaining false positives cluster at rel -3 (D2 of the window's first trial). There prev_common is -1, so the earlier history is unknown and precision is only 0.675. This is a window-truncation artifact and does not refute the explanation.
